questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the first term in the same way as the fourth term is related to the third term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term.

7 : ? :: 15 : 150 :: 18 : 234
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: **First number × (First number - 5) = Second number

15 : 150 → 15 × (15 - 5) = 15 × 10 = 150

18 : 234 → 18 × (18 - 5) = 18 × 13 = 234

Similarly,

7 : ? :: 7 × (7 - 5) = 7 × 2 = 14

Hence, '**14**' is the correct answer.

questions.question:
In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following pairs.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

16, 107

12, 79
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:** (First number × 7) - 5 = Second number

 
• 16, 107 → (16 × 7) - 5 = 112 - 5 = 107
 
• 12, 79 → (12 × 7) - 5 = 84 - 5 = 79

Similarly,

 
• 9, 58 → (9 × 7) - 5 = 63 - 5 = 58

Hence, '**9, 58**' is the correct answer.

questions.question: If 22 September 1982 is Wednesday, then what will be the day of the week on 7 December 1991?
questions.solution:
An ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2 odd days. 

So, the day on the same date for an ordinary year will be 1 day ahead and the day on the same date for a leap year will be 2 days ahead for the next year.

If 22 September 1982 is Wednesday, then the day on these dates will be:

22 September 1983 → Thursday

22 September 1984 → Saturday

22 September 1985 → Sunday

22 September 1986 → Monday

22 September 1987 → Tuesday

22 September 1988 → Thursday

22 September 1989 → Friday

22 September 1990 → Saturday

22 September 1991 → Sunday

Number of days between 22 September to 7 December = (8 + 31 + 30 + 7) = 76

76 when divided by 7, we get 6 as remainder

Sunday + 6 = Saturday

So, it will be Saturday on 7 December 1991.

Hence, ‘**Saturday**’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below.

(The words must be considered meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/consonants/vowels in the word.)

Contain: Hold
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic: **Words are synonyms of each other.

 
• Contain : Hold → Contain is synonym of hold.

Similarly,

 
• Contrast : Disparity → Contrast is synonym of Disparity.

Hence, '**Contrast : Disparity**' is the correct answer.

questions.question: If 21 July 2000 is Friday, then what will be the day of the week on 15 July 2012?
questions.solution:
An ordinary year has 1 odd day and a leap year has 2 odd days. 

So, the day on the same date for an ordinary year will be 1 day ahead and the day on the same date for a leap year will be 2 days ahead for the next year.

If 21 July 2000 is Friday, then the day on these dates will be:

21 July 2001 → Saturday

21 July 2002 → Sunday

21 July 2003 → Monday

21 July 2004 → Wednesday

21 July 2005 → Thursday

21 July 2006 → Friday

21 July 2007 → Saturday

21 July 2008 → Monday

21 July 2009 → Tuesday

21 July 2010 → Wednesday

21 July 2011 → Thursday

21 July 2012 → Saturday

Number of days between 15 July 2012 to 21 July 2012 = 6

Saturday - 6 = Sunday

So, it will be Sunday on 15 July 2012.

Hence, ‘Sunday’ is the correct answer.
